nodes.name: Gamba grass
nodes.desc: A tall tussock grass of West African savannas, recorded often near the park. It is a staple of grazers and carries the dry-season fires.

nodes.name: African ebony
nodes.desc: A savanna and riverine tree whose fruit and leaves are recorded in the diets of antelope, elephants, warthogs and baboons.

nodes.name: Tamarind
nodes.desc: A fruiting savanna tree. GloBI records show its pods and leaves eaten by elephants, antelope, warthogs and baboons.

nodes.name: Isoberlinia doka
nodes.desc: A dominant tree of Sudanian woodland on the deeper soils of the Atakora escarpment, according to Wikipedia. Baboons are recorded eating it.

nodes.name: Kob
nodes.desc: The most-recorded large herbivore near the park, with about 2,600 counted in 2000. It grazes the floodplain and open savanna.

nodes.name: Hartebeest
nodes.desc: A grazing antelope of open savanna; about 1,500 western hartebeest were counted in the park in 2000.

nodes.name: Common warthog
nodes.desc: A pig that grazes short grass and digs for roots and fruit. A frequent prey of lions and hyenas.

nodes.name: Common duiker
nodes.desc: A small, secretive browser that eats leaves, fruit and shoots under woodland cover.

nodes.name: Olive baboon
nodes.desc: An omnivorous primate that eats fruit, seeds and leaves of many savanna trees.

nodes.name: African elephant
nodes.desc: The WAP Complex holds the largest elephant population in West Africa. It browses trees and eats grass, shaping the woodland.

nodes.name: Hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Wikipedia names it the park's second-largest species. It rests in the Pendjari River by day and grazes on land.

nodes.name: African rock python
nodes.desc: A large constrictor recorded in GloBI eating kob and Nile monitors.

nodes.name: Side-striped jackal
nodes.desc: An omnivorous canid that takes small prey, fruit and carrion. It is present in the park.

nodes.name: Spotted hyena
nodes.desc: Hunts antelope and warthog and also scavenges kills. Recorded in the park.

nodes.name: Hooded vulture
nodes.desc: A small scavenging vulture recorded feeding on carcasses of hippo, waterbuck and elephant.

nodes.name: Marabou stork
nodes.desc: A large scavenging stork recorded feeding on carcasses of antelope, hippo and elephant.

nodes.name: Lion
nodes.desc: The WAP Complex may hold West Africa's largest lion population, around 100 in 2009. It preys on antelope, warthog and baboon.

nodes.name: Sun
nodes.desc: Sunlight powers grass and tree growth through the long dry season and the wet season.

nodes.name: Wet-season rain and floods
nodes.desc: About 1,100 mm of rain falls a year, mostly June to November, and the Pendjari River floods seasonally.

nodes.name: Dry-season fire
nodes.desc: UNESCO notes that fire linked to human activity has shaped the vegetation for a very long time, helping maintain habitat diversity.

nodes.name: Savanna soil
nodes.desc: Shallow soils on the rocky cliffs and deeper soils on summits and escarpments support different woodland.

nodes.name: Termites, fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, leaves and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
